clue.text: Our melodic dish cooked with salt

indicators.note: cooked suggests ingredients mixed up and transformed, so the three words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A kitchen boast: our tuneful dish has been prepared with salt.
explanation.definitionFit: Common table salt is the chemical compound of sodium and chlorine, the salt par excellence.

clue.text: This sleuth, he'll shock Morse electrifyingly

indicators.note: an electric jolt throws things about, so the letters of the three words before it are jumbled

explanation.surface: A fictional detective boasts that one great sleuth will startle another, Inspector Morse.
explanation.walkthrough: Morse is another fictional detective, which makes 'Morse' look like part of the definition; it is only anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Conan Doyle's Baker Street consulting detective is the most famous fictional sleuth of all.

clue.text: The stuff of a play

parts.note: a script consists mostly of the characters' spoken exchanges, which is what a play is made of

explanation.surface: What a play is made of.
explanation.definitionFit: Plays are written almost entirely as spoken exchanges between characters, so conversation is their raw material.

clue.text: Horrible fruit caught

indicators.note: caught as in caught by the ear, heard, so the fruit's name is taken by its sound

parts.note: the ugli is a Jamaican citrus fruit, a tangelo

explanation.surface: A horrible piece of fruit has been caught.
explanation.definitionFit: Something horrible to look at is unsightly, hideous.

clue.text: See 1
Vital malfunctions disrupted hackers at Tate endlessly

indicators.note: disrupted means thrown into disorder, so the letters of the fodder are rearranged
endlessly means the word Tate loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Computer hackers break into the Tate gallery's systems and cause chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' trims Tate to TAT, which joins HACKERS and AT for the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardiac arrest is a failure of the heart, an organ vital to life, hence a vital malfunction.

clue.text: No Turkish man will toe the line

parts.note: no, as zero or nothing, is the letter O
a bey is a Turkish governor or gentleman

explanation.surface: A defiant claim that no Turk will conform.
explanation.definitionFit: To toe the line is to conform to rules or orders, to comply with them.

clue.text: Pay no attention to soldier upset about having to accept a negative answer

indicators.note: to accept means to take in, so the answer is placed inside the other pieces
upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the soldier is read backwards

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
re means about, concerning
no is the negative answer

explanation.surface: An irritated soldier is told no and must accept it.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'upset' means turned upside down; 'to accept' places the negative answer between the turned soldier and 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: To disregard something is to pay it no attention.

clue.text: Denigrator dies from alimentary ailment

indicators.note: from here means made out of, so the answer is formed from the rearranged letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A critic dies of a digestive illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is an unusual anagram signal: the answer is made from these letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Anorexia and bulimia are disorders of diet and food intake, so they are illnesses of nourishment, alimentary ailments.

clue.text: Did not start credible sanction

indicators.note: the word for credible loses its opening letter

parts.note: a credible argument is tenable, able to be defended

explanation.surface: A believable penalty was never imposed.
explanation.definitionFit: To sanction something is to authorise or permit it, making it possible.

clue.text: Tease apprentice, maniac for snack food

parts.note: to haze is to bully or tease newcomers with pranks
L is a learner, an apprentice, as on L-plates
a nut is a crazy person, a maniac

explanation.surface: Someone is teasing an apprentice, calling them a maniac.
explanation.definitionFit: The nut of the hazel tree is eaten as a snack, often roasted.

clue.text: Totally bonkers as Alice discovered

parts.note: in Alice's Adventures in Wonderland Alice meets the crazy hatter at the tea party

explanation.surface: Alice found something utterly crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means completely insane, and Carroll's Hatter character, whom Alice meets, embodies it.

clue.text: Flunkey returned spoils

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word for flunkey is read backwards

parts.note: a tool is someone used by others, a lackey or flunkey

explanation.surface: A servant comes back carrying plunder.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoils are goods taken by force, plunder or booty.

clue.text: Beat with stick initially

definitions.meaning: to tack fabric with long loose stitches, holding it together before final sewing

explanation.surface: Hit someone, first using a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are dictionary meanings: to thrash, and to sew with temporary stitches.

clue.text: J.B. Ranson stocking some roughage

indicators.note: stocking means holding in stock, so the name contains the answer within its letters

explanation.surface: A man named J.B. Ranson stocks a little dietary fibre.
explanation.definitionFit: Bran, the husks of cereal grain, is a type of dietary fibre, or roughage.

clue.text: Reference book a sailor returned

indicators.note: returned means going back, so the word for sailor is read backwards

parts.note: an old salt is a seasoned sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor brings back a reference book.
explanation.definitionFit: A book of maps is a standard reference work.

clue.text: Light wood used in herbal salon

indicators.note: used in says the answer is found in the words that follow, spanning both

explanation.surface: A beauty salon specialising in herbs uses lightweight timber.
explanation.definitionFit: Balsa is famously the lightest commercial timber, used for models.

clue.text: Military tribunal punished matriculator

indicators.note: punished suggests being knocked about, so the letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A newly enrolled student is disciplined by a military tribunal.
explanation.definitionFit: A court convened under military law to try members of the armed forces.

clue.text: Not a slave delivered without charge up-front

indicators.note: up-front says the word for without charge goes at the top in this down entry, before the other

parts.note: free means costing nothing
a baby delivered is born

explanation.surface: Someone born free, with no fee paid up front.
explanation.definitionFit: A person born into liberty rather than servitude is not a slave.

clue.text: See 8
Transit stop is area with car and van being damaged

indicators.note: being damaged means knocked out of shape, so the fodder letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A car and van are damaged in a stopover area.
explanation.definitionFit: A caravanserai is an inn where travelling caravans rested on desert routes, a stop in transit.

clue.text: See 1
Base evacuated to accommodate Jack in a French extreme jumping sport

indicators.note: to accommodate means to house, so the remaining pieces go inside
evacuated means emptied, so only the outside letters of the word remain
in places the card for Jack within the French word

parts.note: une is French for a (feminine)
J is the abbreviation for jack in cards

explanation.surface: A base jumper makes room for a man called Jack in a French extreme sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evacuated' keeps only the outer letters of Base; une is the feminine French for 'a'. This spelling is a less common variant of the usual one with a G.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaping from a height attached to an elastic cord is the classic extreme jumping sport.

clue.text: The burden old star rejected

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the word for star is read backwards

parts.note: the sun is our star

explanation.surface: An old star was rejected under the burden of age.
explanation.definitionFit: An onus is a duty or responsibility, a burden.

clue.text: At the end of day, to stare and gape is awkward

parts.note: to gawk is to stare stupidly, gaping

indicators.note: the final letter of day is taken and placed at the end

explanation.surface: By nightfall, gawping and staring seems clumsy.
explanation.definitionFit: A gangly, clumsy person is ungainly, which is a synonym of awkward.

clue.text: First person to be upset during party protest

indicators.note: during means within, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: to be upset means turned over, so the pronoun is read backwards

parts.note: me is the first-person pronoun

explanation.surface: Someone is the first to get upset at a party protest.
explanation.definitionFit: A demo is short for demonstration, a public protest march or rally.

clue.text: Streaker getting arse kicked violently during trip

indicators.note: kicked means thrown out, and violently means stirred up, so arse is removed and what is left is rearranged

explanation.surface: A streaker is kicked in the backside on an outing.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove A, R, S, E from STREAKER to leave T, K, R, E, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A trek is a long or arduous journey, a trip.

clue.text: Star lover whose lamp went out tragically

definitions.meaning: the principal character of a story or film

definitions.text: lover whose lamp went out tragically
definitions.meaning: in Greek myth Leander swam the Hellespont nightly guided by his beloved's lamp; it blew out and he drowned

explanation.surface: A star-crossed lover's lamp went out tragically.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are fair: the leading figure of a story, and the priestess of Sestos loved by Leander.

clue.text: More than half reached the age of consent

definitions.meaning: the larger number, over fifty percent
legal adulthood, the age at which one may act on one's own behalf

explanation.surface: Over half have come of age.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the greater part of a group and full legal age.

clue.text: Look at husband in admonition to grow up

indicators.note: in places the husband's letter inside the admonition

parts.note: be old is a jokey urging to act one's age

explanation.surface: Look at the husband being told to grow up.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic imperative meaning see or observe.

clue.text: Heckling pack or sneerers at this part of Hyde Park

indicators.note: heckling suggests disruption, so the letters of the words that follow are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A crowd of jeering hecklers gathers at a famous spot in Hyde Park.
explanation.definitionFit: The north-east corner of Hyde Park, a London royal park, is where anyone may stand and make public addresses.
